name: Phil's Curry
ingredients: 220g/7¾oz cherry tomatoes on the vine, halved
2cm/¾in fresh root ginger, peeled and grated
1 tsp sea salt, plus extra if needed
200g/7oz basmati rice, rinsed and drained well
method: To make the curry, preheat the oven to 200C/180C Fan/Gas 6.

Tip the tomatoes on the vines, the green pepper, onion, ginger, garlic, spices, curry leaves (if using), salt and oil into a roasting tin and mix really well to coat everything evenly. Roast for 15–20 minutes (if your oven runs hot and things start to char, rescue them after 15).
Fish out the vines, squash down the tomatoes, add the coconut milk, prawns and spinach and return to the oven for 9–10 minutes, or until the prawns are pink and just cooked through.

Meanwhile, make the rice. Place the rice and 400ml/14fl oz boiling water in a large glass microwave-safe bowl. Cover with a microwave-safe plate that neatly covers the top of the bowl to act as a lid. Microwave on medium power (800W) for 11 minutes. Leave to stand for 10 minutes.
Taste and season the curry with the lime juice and more salt if needed. Scatter over the coriander and chilli and serve with the rice alongside.

name: M&S Curry
ingredients: 1 carrot, grated - no need to peel
method: Preheat the oven to 180°C/160°C fan/gas mark 4.
Heat a splash of oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the Bombay-style spice paste (1 jar), keeping the jar, and fry the paste for a few minutes, until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes (2), lentils (200 g), and carrot (1). Cover with water and season. Bring to the boil, then simmer, covered, for around 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, place the chickpeas (1 tin) into a small baking tray. Drizzle a little oil into the used jar of Bombay-style spice paste, shake, then pour the flavoured oil over the chickpeas. Season and scatter over the chilli flakes (1 tsp), then roast in the oven for 10 minutes.
Add the kale (75 g) and roast for another 5-10 minutes until everything is nice and crispy.
Cook the rice (200 g) according to the packet instructions.
When the lentils are done, stir in the spinach (120 g) and simmer for a few minutes until it's cooked through. Season to taste, adding a squeeze of lemon juice (1/2) if needed.

Heat a little oil in a small frying pan over a medium heat, then add the green chillies (2), cumin seeds (1 tsp) and mustard seeds (1 tsp). Sizzle for a couple of minutes until fragrant, then add to the dahl.
Serve the dahl topped with the crispy kale and chickpeas and alongside the rice. Add some fresh coriander (1 handful), if you like.

name: Max's Curry
ingredients: ½ medium butternut squash, peeled and cut into 1cm (½in) dice
2-3tbsp Greek-style yoghurt, plus extra to serve
method: Sauté the onion and garlic in the oil in a lidded saucepan until soft. Add the ginger and spices.
Cook, stirring, for 2 mins.
Add the stock, tomato and butternut squash, and simmer uncovered for 15 mins.
Add the cauliflower, cover and simmer for 10 mins, or until tender. To serve, stir in the yoghurt and fresh coriander. Serve hot with naan bread and extra yogurt, if desired.

name: Christmas Turkey
ingredients: 1 x 5 kg just under 12lb, Bronze turkey
salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Pre heat the oven to 200°C gas 6.
Chop all the vegetables into large chunks and place in the bottom of a large baking tray place the turkey on top, the tray should be large enough so the bird has at least 2 inches gap around.
Pour in the white wine, cold water and chicken stock cube, and place the whole tray on to the stove.
Bring to the boil and cover tightly with two layers of foil and pop into a preheated oven.
cook the bird for about 2 hours, approximately.
To check if the bird is cooked, remove from the oven carefully as there will be a lot of stock, wine and turkey juices.
Remove the foil and insert a knife where the thigh attaches itself to the body of the bird, the juices should run clear. If not, then cover again with foil and cook for a further 20 minutes.
When the bird is cooked, remove from the oven, turn the oven up to 230 degrees C, Gas 8, brush with the melted butter and cook until browned, about 15 minutes.
When nicely browned, remove from the oven and carefully, tip off all the stock and keep warm.
Wrap the turkey in foil to keep warm, it will keep perfectly wrapped for 1 hour.
Re boil the stock and juices, you may need to add a little more water in a saucepan and skim well.
Mix the cornflour and water together and thicken the bubbling stock, don't go mad.
Carve the bird the flesh will be soft and juicy, and serve the gravy and stuffing separately.
Please remember that times will depend on each individual oven, but the most important thing is that you seal the turkey well (use a tin with a lip) with foil so that you steam the bird.

name: Turkish-Spiced Griddled Chicken with Hot Green Relish
ingredients: 2 garlic cloves, grated to a purée
Leaves from 8 sprigs of mint, torn (for the relish)
70g pitted green olives, roughly chopped (for the relish)
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (for the relish)
2 tbsp white balsamic vinegar (for the relish)
Good squeeze of lemon juice, plus lemon wedges to serve (for the relish)
method: Put half the chicken thighs between two pieces of greaseproof paper or baking parchment. Bash them with a rolling pin so that you end up with fillets that are of an even thickness. Do the same with the other three fillets.

Mix the oil, spices, garlic and some salt and pepper together for the marinade. Put the chicken into a dish and pour over the marinade, turning the fillets to coat them. Cover with cling film and refrigerate for a couple of hours or overnight. Bring them out of the fridge before cooking so that they're not cold.

Make the relish just before you cook the chicken. Crush the garlic with the sea salt with a pestle and mortar (or grate it to a purée). Halve and deseed both chillies and chop roughly. Add to the mortar with the coriander, mint and olives and bash everything together, gradually adding the oil and balsamic until you have a paste (it should be chunky, not puréed). Add lemon juice to taste and set aside.

Heat a griddle until hot. Lift the chicken out of the marinade, shaking off the excess, and cook on a medium heat for about two minutes on each side, then reduce the heat to low and cook for a further 2 minutes on each side. The chicken should be cooked through and singed in places, but not burnt.
Serve with lemon wedges, rice, bulgur or flatbread, a bowl of Greek yogurt and the relish.

name: Porcini orzotto
ingredients: 5g parmesan (or veggie eqivalent), finely grated, plus extra to serve
method: Rehydrate the dried porcini in 500ml of freshly boiled water for 20 minutes, while simultaneously halving half of the button mushrooms, thinly slicing the remainder, and slicing the garlic.

Heat oil in a pan until very hot, then sauté the garlic and fresh mushrooms until the sliced ones become golden and crispy. Stir in a little salt, thyme, and the white wine, reducing the heat and allowing the liquid to cook down by half.

Concurrently, toast the dry orzo in another pan over medium heat until lightly browned. Drain the soaked porcini, reserving the steeping liquid, and carefully pour this liquid into the toasted orzo, taking care to discard any sediment. Simmer the pasta for approximately 10 minutes.

Dice the soaked porcini and mix them into the cooked button mushrooms. Once the orzo has absorbed the liquid and become tender (add water if it needs more time), remove from heat. Combine the cooked orzo with the mushroom mixture, mascarpone, and parmesan, then cover and rest for 5 minutes. Finish by seasoning with salt, pepper, and a squeeze of lemon, and garnish with the fresh herbs and more cheese before serving.

name: Homemade Pita Bread
ingredients: 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, plus more for the bowl
method: Make sponge: In a large mixing bowl add 1 cup lukewarm water and stir in yeast and sugar until dissolved. Add 1/2 cup flour and whisk together. Place the mixing bowl in a warm place, uncovered to form a loose sponge. Give it 15 minutes or so, the mixture should bubble.

Form the pita dough: Add salt, olive oil and almost all the remaining flour (keep about 1/2 cup of the flour for dusting later). Stir until mixture forms a shaggy mass. Dust with a little flour, then knead the mixture inside the bowl for about a minute to incorporate any stray bits.

Knead the dough: Dust a clean working surface with a little bit of flour. Knead lightly for a couple minutes until smooth. Cover and let the dough rest for 10 minutes, then knead again for a couple more minutes.

Let the dough rise: Clean the mixing bowl and coat it lightly with extra virgin olive oil and put the dough back in the bowl. Turn the dough a couple times to coat with the olive oil. Cover tightly with plastic wrap then lay a kitchen towel over. Put in a warm place for 1 hour or until doubled in size.
Divide the dough: Deflate the dough and place on a clean work surface. Divide into 7 to 8 equal pieces and shape into balls. Cover with a towel and leave for 10 minutes to rest.
Shape the pitas: Using a floured rolling pin, roll one of the pieces into a circle that's 8-9 inches wide and about a quarter inch thick. Repeat with the other pieces of dough.

To bake in the oven: Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) and place a heavy-duty baking pan or large cast iron skillet on the middle rack to heat. Working in batches, place the rolled-out pitas directly on the hot baking sheet. Bake for 2 minutes on one side, then carefully turn over to bake for 1 minute on the other side. Remove and cover with a clean towel.

To cook on stovetop: Heat a cast iron skillet over medium-high heat. Lay a rolled-out pita on the skillet and bake for 30 seconds, until bubbles start to form. Flip the pita over and cook for 1-2 minutes on the other side. Flip again and cook another 1-2 minutes to toast the other side. Keep baked pita covered with a clean towel.

name: Ridiculously e=Easy Flatbreads
method: Mix the flour, yoghurt, and salt in a bowl using your hands to form a soft dough. Adjust with extra flour if it feels too sticky, or extra yoghurt if it feels dry.
Transfer the dough to a floured surface, gently shape it into a smooth ball, and divide it into 6 or 8 equal triangular pieces.
Preheat a dry frying pan.
Roll each piece out thinly. If you are using seeds, press them into the dough during this rolling stage.
Cook each flatbread individually in the hot pan until they puff up and develop brown spots on both sides.

name: French Beans with Sun-Dried Tomatoes, Feta and Mozzarella
ingredients: 70g drained and sliced sun-dried tomatoes in oil
2 drained buffalo mozzarella balls, cut into chunks
method: Remove the ends from the beans and boil them in salted water for roughly 5 minutes until tender but firm, then drain well and place into a serving bowl.
While still warm, combine the beans with the tomatoes, walnuts, olive oil, and lemon juice, adding seasoning to taste before leaving to cool.
Break the feta into pieces and stir it into the mixture along with the chopped mozzarella, then serve right away.

name: Posh Fish and (Chunky) Chips
ingredients: 500g scrubbed small-medium potatoes, such as Maris Piper
Large pinch of dried oregano or thyme
4 x 140g skinned white fish fillets (e.g., cod or haddock)
Tartare sauce or vinegar for serving
method: Warm your oven to 220C/Gas 7 and prepare a large baking tray with a lip.

Slice the potatoes in half and then into wedges. Toss them in a bowl with a splash of olive oil, oregano or thyme, and salt. Spread them evenly on the tray, cut-side down, and roast for 15-18 minutes until golden.
Blend or mix together the breadcrumbs, parmesan, olive oil, salt, and pepper to create the crust mixture.

Arrange the fish fillets evenly among the roasted potatoes, tucking under any thin edges for even cooking. Cover the tops of the fish with the parmesan crust and return the tray to the top of the oven for 5-7 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Place the samphire in a heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and toss with butter if desired. Serve the samphire alongside the baked fish and chips.

name: Coriander and Mint Grilled Meaty Skewers
ingredients: 6 skinless boneless chicken or turkey breasts, cubed
method: Blend the lemon juice, yogurt, spices, honey, and herbs together until smooth to create a marinade.
Place the cubed meat in a bowl, season well, and pour the blended mixture over the top. Toss to ensure everything is coated, then cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 30 minutes.
Heat up your grill. Thread the marinated meat onto skewers and cook for 10-12 minutes, turning them regularly to ensure they cook evenly throughout.
Serve the hot skewers garnished with extra mint leaves, accompanied by lemon wedges and a side salad.

name: Pasta Ribbons with Prawns and Rocket
ingredients: 1 medium-hot red chilli, deseeded and sliced
300g large fresh raw prawns (peeled, heads and tails removed)
method: Warm the olive oil in a pan and briefly fry the garlic, pine nuts, and chilli for 20 seconds. Toss in the prawns and cook until they change color.
Pour in the white wine, add the basil, and season. Let the mixture bubble over high heat for approximately 2 minutes before taking the pan off the heat.
Boil the linguine in salted water until just tender, then drain it and mix it directly into the pan with the prawns. Place back over high heat, stir in the rocket leaves, and serve immediately.

name: Crunchy Tandoori Chicken with Home-Made Minty Slaw
ingredients: 8 skinless chicken thigh fillets, visible fat trimmed
method: Mix the curry powder, a pinch of salt, and the yogurt in a large bowl. Add the chicken pieces, ensuring they are fully coated, and leave to marinate for at least half an hour.
Heat your oven to 220C/200C fan/Gas 7. Crush the cornflakes into a fine crumb consistency.
Prepare a baking tray with foil and a generous spray of cooking oil. Take each piece of marinated chicken, shake off excess yogurt, and roll it in the crushed cornflakes until coated.
Arrange the coated chicken on the tray, spray the tops with cooking spray, and bake for 25 minutes. Check them around the 20-minute mark to ensure the crust isn't burning.
While the chicken bakes, prepare the slaw by tossing the cabbage, carrots, spring onions, lemon juice, and mint together in a bowl, seasoning to taste.
Ensure the chicken is golden and cooked through with clear juices, then serve hot alongside the freshly made slaw.

name: Beef, Kale & Cashew Stir Fry in Oyster Sauce
method: Bring a saucepan of water to the boil and cook the noodles for 4 minutes, then drain and cool under cold running water. Toss with 1 tbsp groundnut or vegetable oil and set aside. Meanwhile, cut the steak into 0.5cm slices, season and put in a mixing bowl with the soy sauce, sesame oil, oyster sauce and garlic; set aside.

Cut the salad onions into 2cm lengths. Remove and discard the woody kale stalks and roughly chop the leaves. Put a wok or large frying pan over a medium heat, then toast the cashews for a few minutes until lightly golden; set aside on a plate. Return the pan to the hob, turn up the heat and add 1 tbsp oil. Fry the salad onions and kale for 5 minutes until charred and lightly cooked; transfer to a plate. Bring a kettle to the boil. Put the pan back on the hob, add the remaining 2 tbsp oil and the marinated steak, leaving the marinade in the bowl. Cook the steak for 3 minutes over a high heat until browned on all surfaces.

Meanwhile, stir the cornflour into the bowl with the marinade and add 3 tbsp just-boiled water. Return the cashews, kale and salad onions to the pan and pour in the steak marinade. Stir fry for 2 more minutes, then stir in the noodles. Fry for 2-3 minutes more, adding a splash more boiling water if needed, until everything is piping hot, glossy and coated. Serve straight away.

name: Pulled Beef Brisket
ingredients: 200ml/7fl oz cooking juices from the beef brisket or beef gravy
15g/0.5oz fresh yeast or 1 x 7g sachet of fast-action yeast
method: Lightly toast the whole spices (coriander, cumin, mustard seeds, and peppercorns) in a pan, then grind them into a powder and stir in the sugar, paprika, and cayenne.
Make incisions in the brisket and massage the spice blend all over it, then tie it up securely with string, wrap it in cling film, and let it marinate in the refrigerator overnight.

The following day, bake the beef on a rack placed inside a roasting tin with the stock poured around it; cover tightly with foil and cook at 160C/325F/Gas 3 for 4 to 6 hours until tender, adding water if the pan dries out.
Let the cooked beef rest in its foil for 25 minutes, making sure to save the cooking liquids.

To make the buns, place the flour in a mixer equipped with a dough hook, keeping the yeast separated from the salt and sugar; pour in the gently warmed milk and butter, and knead for about 5 to 8 minutes until smooth and shiny.
Let the covered dough rise in a warm spot for 1 to 2 hours until it doubles in size, then knock the air out and divide it into 12 equal 80g portions shaped into balls.
Place the dough balls on oiled baking sheets, cover with greased cling film, and let them rise again for an hour until they expand and touch each other.
Glaze the risen buns with the beaten egg, top with sesame seeds and sea salt, and bake at 220C/425F/Gas 7 for 8 to 12 minutes until golden brown.

For the barbecue sauce, boil and reduce the vinegar by half in a large pan, then mix in the sugar, bourbon, cola, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and the skimmed beef juices, simmering gently for 15 to 20 minutes.
Shred the rested beef brisket with forks, combine it with the simmering barbecue sauce, and cook together for a final 10 to 15 minutes before serving inside the baked milk buns.

name: Naan Bread
ingredients: 300g strong white bread flour, plus extra for dusting
25g butter or ghee, melted, plus extra 2-3 tbsp for brushing
method: Combine 125ml warm water, yeast, and 1 tsp of the sugar in a bowl, resting it until it bubbles for about 10-15 minutes. In a separate bowl, blend the flour, remaining sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, and baking powder. Form a well and incorporate the yeast liquid, melted butter, yogurt, and seeds. Mix by hand into a soft dough, adjusting with water or flour as needed.

Knead the mixture briefly in the bowl before moving to a floured counter. Continue kneading for 10 minutes until elastic and smooth. Place the dough ball into a greased bowl, cover it, and let it rise in a warm spot for about an hour until doubled in size.

Split the risen dough into six portions and rest them on a floured tray under a damp cloth. Warm a dry non-stick pan over high heat. Roll a dough portion into a 21cm by 13cm teardrop shape. Cook in the hot pan for 3 minutes, flip, and cook the reverse side for 3-4 minutes until charred patches appear.
Transfer the finished flatbreads to a low oven to stay warm. Brush each one with the extra melted butter or ghee, stacking them and keeping them covered with foil while you finish the rest.

name: Nachos
ingredients: salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Get the oven hot, setting it to 200C (180C Fan or Gas Mark 6). In a skillet on medium heat, warm the oil and sauté the onions for 3 to 5 minutes until they become tender and translucent.
Turn up the stove temperature, adding the minced beef and the dried spices to the pan. Fry the mixture for 5 to 10 minutes, stirring periodically, until the meat is completely browned.
Lower the heat back to a medium setting and mix in the black beans. Stir carefully until the beans are hot, then season the mix with salt and black pepper.

Grab a 1.5-litre baking dish and spread out a base layer of tortilla chips. Spoon half of your cooked meat mixture over the chips, followed by half of the cheese and half of the tomatoes. Repeat this process with another layer of chips, the rest of the beef, and the remaining cheese. Bake this in the hot oven for 8 to 10 minutes to melt the cheese.

Take the dish out of the oven and garnish it with the rest of the fresh tomatoes, chopped spring onions, and any optional chillies or coriander. Serve immediately alongside lime wedges and soured cream.

name: Lamb, Kale & Ginger Curry
ingredients: Cooked basmati rice and/or naan breads, to serve[cite: 23]
method: Cut the lamb into 3cm chunks. Put a casserole dish or large saucepan over a high heat and add 1 tbsp ghee and the lamb. Season, then fry for 10 minutes until the lamb is browned all over. Transfer the lamb to a plate; set aside. Reduce the heat to medium and add the cumin seeds, cinnamon and bay leaf. Fry for 1 minute, then add the remaining 2 tbsp ghee, the garlic, ginger, ½ of the sliced chillies, the ground turmeric, chilli powder, garam masala and onions. Lower the heat a little more and sauté for 10 minutes until the onions are softening. Stir in the tomato purée, then add the browned lamb.[cite: 23]

Pour in 400ml water and season, then bring to the boil, cover and reduce to a simmer. Cook for 1½-2 hours, or until the lamb is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly. Remove the lid for the final 20 minutes of cooking if the sauce still looks thin.[cite: 23]

While the lamb is cooking, bring a large pan of water to the boil and cook the kale for 5 minutes. Drain and transfer to a bowl of cold water. Once the kale is cool, drain again and whizz in a blender until smooth, adding 1-2 tbsp water to make a thick purée. When the lamb is ready, stir in the kale purée. Cook for a further 5-10 minutes, uncovered, until the sauce is rich and thickened; season if needed. Scatter over the remaining sliced chillies and serve with fluffy basmati rice and/or naan breads.[cite: 23]

name: Prawn & Courgette Pasta with Lemongrass
ingredients: 2 fresh lemongrass stalks, woody ends trimmed and tough outer leaves removed[cite: 24]
150g pack cooked Waitrose & Partners Extra Large King Prawns[cite: 24]
½ lemon, juice, plus extra wedges to serve[cite: 24]
method: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Pare the courgettes into thin strips with a vegetable peeler (or use a julienne peeler or spiraliser); set aside. Add the pasta to the boiling water and cook according to pack instructions.[cite: 24]

Meanwhile, chop the lemongrass as finely as possible. Tip into a frying pan with the oil, garlic and salt, and set over a medium-low heat. As the oil warms, it will gently cook the garlic and lemongrass; after 4-5 minutes it should be fragrant and lightly golden. Add the chilli flakes and prawns, and heat for 1 minute more. Squeeze in the lemon juice.[cite: 24]

Drain the pasta and immediately add to the pan with the prawns. Take off the heat and toss everything together. Cool for a couple of minutes, then toss through the courgettes and coriander. Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing over.[cite: 24]

name: Highland Pasta with Smoked Salmon
ingredients: 4 oz (110 g) dried pasta (such as macaroni, penne or rigatoni)[cite: 25]
1 clove garlic, crushed with ½ teaspoon salt[cite: 25]
4 oz (110 g) chestnut mushrooms, thinly sliced[cite: 25]
5 fl oz (150 ml) dry white wine[cite: 25]
method: Begin by melting the butter in a solid-based frying pan, then add the onion and sauté over a low heat until soft. This will take about 7 minutes. Now add the crushed garlic and mushrooms and continue to cook for a further 2-3 minutes. Next, mix the curry powder and flour together and stir these into the butter to soak up all the juices. Then add the wine gradually, stirring briskly after each addition and, when all the wine is added, cook for a further 3 minutes before finally adding the crème fraîche. The sauce is now ready and can be made up to this stage in advance, but lay a piece of clingfilm over the surface if you're not using it immediately.[cite: 25]

When you're ready to cook the pasta, place a large saucepan with plenty of lightly salted water on to boil and cook the pasta for 10-12 minutes or until it is cooked to your liking, but still retains some bite. Meanwhile, tear little pieces of smoked salmon lengthways into strips, then re-heat the sauce and add the salmon at the very last minute, just before serving. Now, drain the pasta, return it to the pan, then quickly stir in the sauce and smoked salmon and serve at once in deep, heated bowls.[cite: 25]

name: Fajitas
method: Slice protein and vegetables.
Marinade protein in seasonings for ~2 hours before cooking.
Fry protein in a splash of oil until browned.
Add peppers, onion, mushroom and leftover seasoning.
Heat tortillas for 30s in microwave on full power.
Serve with grated cheese, guacamole, and salsa.
